'''Nagahatabe Shrine (Hitachiota)''' is a shrine in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Hitachi Province]].

'''Nagahatabe Shrine''' (長幡部神社, Nagahatabe Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto shrine|qq=}} located in [[Hitachiota]], [[Ibaraki Prefecture]]. It is listed as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} and was Ranked as a village shrine under the [[modern shrine Ranking system]].

== Deities ==
The shrine enshrines the following two deities, considered ancestral gods of the Nagahatabe clan according to the {{ill|Hitachi Fudoki|ja|常陸国風土記|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hitachi Fudoki|qq=}}<ref name="ShrineHistory">Shrine's historical documents.</ref>:
* '''Kihime-no-Mikoto''' (綺日女命)
* '''Tate-no-Mikoto''' (多弖命)

== History ==
=== About Nagahatabe ===
The term "Nagahata" refers to a type of silk fabric called {{ill|Ashiginu|ja|絁|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ashiginu|qq=}}, and the "Nagahatabe" represents a group of artisans skilled in weaving this fabric<ref name="Deities"/>. Historical records such as the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nihon Shoki|qq=}} and {{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kojiki|qq=}} indicate that the Nagahatabe clan may have roots in both imperial and immigrant lineages. According to the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|ja|新撰姓氏録|1=Shinsen Shōjiroku|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinsen Shōjiroku|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinsen Shōjiroku|qq=}}, one lineage traces its origin to the immigrant "Seven Surnamed Han People" led by {{ill|Achi no Omi|ja|阿知使主|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Achi no Omi|qq=}}<ref name="Deities"/>.

=== Foundation ===
The shrine's foundation is described in the {{ill|Hitachi Fudoki|ja|常陸国風土記|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hitachi Fudoki|qq=}}, which states that Kihime-no-Mikoto accompanied {{ill|Ninigi|ja|ニニギ|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninigi|qq=}} on his descent from the heavens and later moved to Hitachi under the guidance of Tate-no-Mikoto during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|ja|崇神天皇|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Sujin|qq=}}. It is believed that Tate-no-Mikoto established a weaving facility and began the practice of weaving at this location.

=== Later History ===
According to the {{ill|Jinshin Jitsuroku|ja|日本文徳天皇実録|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jinshin Jitsuroku|qq=}}, the shrine received a Rank of Senior Sixth Rank Upper in {{ill|Ninju|ja|仁寿|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninju|qq=}} 1 (851). The {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|qq=}} lists it as "Nagahatabe Shrine" under {{ill|Kujigun|ja|久慈郡|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kujigun|qq=}} in Hitachi Province<ref group="note">Another shrine with the same name, Nagahatabe Shrine, is listed in Musashi Province.</ref>.

During the {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Heian period|qq=}}, {{ill|Minamoto no Yoriyoshi|ja|源頼義|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Minamoto no Yoriyoshi|qq=}} prayed for victory at this shrine during his campaign and dedicated a flag. Later, the shrine's prominence declined, and it was renamed several times, including "Komaata Shrine." In the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Edo period|qq=}}, the shrine was restored to its original name "Nagahatabe Shrine" based on oral traditions.

In the {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治|lt=Meiji period|1=Meiji era|2=ja|3=明治|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}}, the shrine was Ranked as a village shrine in the modern shrine Ranking system<ref name="ShrineHistory"/>.

== Related Sites ==
* '''Former Shrine Site:''' Located about 700 meters northwest of the current location.
* '''Hata Yama Kofun Cluster:''' A group of Kofuns on the shrine's grounds, designated as a historic site by Hitachiota City.

== Festivals ==
The shrine holds several annual festivals, including:
* '''New Year Festival''' (January 1)<ref>Shrine's historical documents.</ref>
* '''Prayer Festival''' (February 20)
* '''Spring Festival''' (April 9)
* '''Autumn Festival''' (Lunisolar September 29)
* '''Harvest Festival''' (November 30)

== Current Information ==
'''Address:'''
539 Hata-cho, Hitachiota, Ibaraki Prefecture

'''Nearby:'''
